script.speaker: Richard
script.text:
Two agents handed off a task, and the run passed. What did the handoff leave out?

> worth scaled by gauge (hundredths/100, thousandth*1000, plain pass)

That line is the whole handoff for scaling values, from a public four-agent run: message 5484, backend agent to UI agent. It names three cases. [Read the handoff ↗](https://github.com/null-hype/agent-plugins/blob/39e328c5206642c1de53bca42f7014b93c9a3602/examples/yoars-handoff/pairs/msg5484-summarize.json#L16)

script.speaker: UI agent · handoff only
script.text:
> **Unknown gauge value:** is the row passed through unscaled, dropped, or does it raise an error?

It sensed a gap, but couldn't say which answer was right.

script.speaker: UI agent · with delta-zero
script.text:
> The backend assumed this case "will be dropped anyway since epoch/person empty". The code doesn't do that. A line with a missing or unknown `u=` gets **kept, with `worth` not converted**.

It quoted the code, found that a non-numeric amount crashes `normalize()`, and held back its sign-off. [Both replies, verbatim ↗](https://github.com/null-hype/agent-plugins/blob/39e328c5206642c1de53bca42f7014b93c9a3602/examples/yoars-handoff/AGENT-RUN.md)

script.speaker: Richard
script.text:
I built delta-zero to catch that. It checks each handoff against the conversation behind it and quotes what was dropped, right in the editor.

![VS Code: delta-zero's finding m35-dropped in the Problems panel, with its evidence open at the backend's dropped note](/evidence/handoff-5484-vscode.png)

[The source line ↗](https://github.com/null-hype/agent-plugins/blob/39e328c5206642c1de53bca42f7014b93c9a3602/examples/yoars-handoff/pairs/msg5484-full.json) · [VS Code extension ↗](https://github.com/null-hype/agent-plugins/pull/427)
